list.name: controller_instance
list.label: Controller
list.description: Which WVA controller emitted the series. A cluster runs one per namespace-scoped install; this is how an admin tells them apart.

panels.title: Fleet health — all namespaces
panels.description: Controller and cluster health. These panels do NOT follow the Namespace variable: they answer "is WVA working", across every namespace it manages.

panels.title: WVA installs present
panels.description: WVA controller Deployments on the cluster, from kube-state-metrics. Compare with the next panel: a gap means an install exists but is not being scraped.

panels.title: Controllers reporting metrics
panels.description: Distinct controllers whose metrics reach Prometheus. Lower than 'installs present' means some install is not scraped -- a broken ServiceMonitor looks exactly like a controller that is not scaling.

panels.title: WVA scrape targets DOWN
panels.description: Scrape targets Prometheus cannot reach. Anything above zero is an install whose panels below will be silently empty.

panels.title: Namespaces being optimized
panels.description: Namespaces with at least one WVA-managed variant reporting.
Optimization interval
panels.title: Optimization Interval (Secs)

panels.description: Indicates whether GPU discovery is on or off. WVA only discovers GPUs when a gpu-inventory limiter is declared in the saturation config's "limiters" list. Related metric is wva_available_gpus. Metric is wva_gpu_discovery_up.
panels.title: GPU Discovery Status

panels.description: Number of available GPUs by accelerator type. When wva_gpu_discovery_up metric is 1, shows number of currently available GPUs. When wva_gpu_discovery_up is 0, shows the number of GPUs that were available at the last successful discovery. Only available in clusters such as OpenShift where WVA can iterate over node objects. There is no exclusions such as tainted nodes or GPUs operating in different modes such as MIG. Metric is wva_available_gpus.
panels.title: Available GPUs

panels.description: Number of models processed in the last optimization cycle. A variant is found when KEDA calls WVA's external scaler for its ScaledObject, whose trigger metadata carries the modelID. Metric is wva_models_processed.
panels.title: Models Processed

panels.description: Number of new errors by component in the last hour. Shows how many errors occurred in the past 60 minutes. Resets to 0 once errors age beyond the 1-hour window. Metric is wva_errors_total.
panels.title: WVA Errors

panels.description: Freshness status of metrics for each variant. "fresh": metric collected < 1 minute ago, "stale": metric collected < 5 minutes ago, "unavailable": metric collected >= 5 minutes ago, "missing": metric doesn't exist. wva_metrics_freshness_status.
panels.title: Metrics Freshness

panels.description: Number of metrics collection errors during the last hour. Metric is wva_metrics_collection_errors_total.
panels.title: Metric Collection Errors

panels.description: Duration of metrics collection operations by query type in seconds. Metric is wva_metrics_collection_duration_seconds.
panels.title: Metrics Collection Duration - Percentiles and Average

panels.description: Duration of optimization loop cycles in seconds. Metric is wva_optimization_duration_seconds.
panels.title: Optimization Duration - Percentiles and Average
Selected namespace: $namespace
panels.description: What WVA did to the workloads in the selected namespace. Every panel here follows the Namespace variable.

panels.title: Queued but unmeasured
panels.description: Requests queued at engines the collector could not measure, in the selected namespace. Broken down per model in the chart of the same name below.

panels.title: Models blocked from scaling
panels.description: Models the optimizer decided not to scale, in the selected namespace, each counted once. The utilization-share optimizer's passing states (awaiting-release, reversal-hold, swinging, transfer-limit) and floor-pinned are not counted: they are expected while it works. Every reason is in the 'Models that will not scale, by reason' chart below.

Pod-to-variant mapping misses in the selected namespace over the last hour.

Absence of the series means no miss ever happened, so this reads 0 rather than 'No data' -- which on a counter is the same fact told twice as ambiguously. Not applied to the two error gauges beside it: they group by component and query_type, and `or vector(0)` appends an unlabelled zero series next to the real ones (measured on Thanos).
panels.title: Pod Mapping Misses

panels.description: Number of pods with metrics discovered for a namespace. Metric is wva_metrics_pods_discovered.
panels.title: Pods with Metrics
Queued but unmeasured, by model
panels.description: Which model is queueing without a measurable replica, and for how long. A flat non-zero line is an autoscaler that will never react: the demand is real and no variant carries it.

panels.title: Models that will not scale, by reason
panels.description: One line per (model, reason) for as long as the reason holds; the series disappears when it is resolved, so a flat line is a standing condition nobody has acted on. variant-floor: scale-to-zero is enabled but a variant declares minReplicas > 0, so the model never reaches zero and the setting is inert. policy-forbids-zero: every variant permits zero but the model's policy disables scale-to-zero, so the bounds are inert - most misleading with a single variant. engine-unsupported: the model runs both vLLM and SGLang, so no single request counter measures its idleness (either alone is supported). activation-retention: just woken from zero and held for the retention period so the wake is not undone -- transient, and clears itself. no-wake-signal: EPP is exporting no flow-control queue at all, so nothing can wake a parked model - usually an EPP pod older than the ConfigMap that enabled flowControl.

panels.title: Models at zero replicas
panels.description: Total replicas serving each model, summed across its variants. Zero is normal for an idle model that scaled to zero, and a fault only when demand exists - which is what the WVAModelParkedWhileRequestsRefused alert joins against, using this series as the key. EPP's request metrics carry model_name and no namespace, and the per-variant wva_current_replicas carries no model_name, so this is the only series the two sides can be joined on. A line sitting flat at zero while traffic arrives is a stranded model.

KV cache token usage vs capacity. wva_kv_cache_tokens_used: Total KV cache tokens currently in use across all replicas of a variant (sum of vLLM TokensInUse). wva_kv_cache_tokens_capacity: Total KV cache token capacity across all replicas of a variant (sum of vLLM TotalKvCapacityTokens).
panels.title: Capacity Breakdown
Variants pinned at their ceiling
panels.description: 1 while a variant's target sits on its own maxReplicas. On its own this is unremarkable - a correctly sized variant sits at its ceiling under load. It matters together with utilization above the scale-up threshold, which is demand going unserved: the remedy there is to raise maxReplicas, NOT to add accelerators (that is wva_decisions_limited_total, which means GPUs ran out). Also read it when interpreting a benchmark - a run pinned at its ceiling measures the ceiling, not the autoscaler.

Per-variant utilization ratio from saturation analysis: TotalDemand / TotalCapacity from the analyzer result. Capacity-weighted and unbounded above — a value > 1.0 means demand exceeds supply. wva_saturation_utilization.
panels.title: Saturation Utilization

panels.description: Replica count comparison. wva_current_replicas: Current number of replicas for each variant. wva_desired_replicas: Desired number of replicas for each variant.
panels.title: Replica Overview

panels.description: Number of scaling operations per second over the last 5 minutes, grouped by decision reason. Metric is wva_replica_scaling_total.
panels.title: Scaling Decision Rate

panels.description: Average number of scaling decisions limited by constraints per optimization cycle (averaged over 1 hour). Shows how often limiters prevent scaling due to insufficient capacity. For example, there were 36 limited decisions total in the last hour for 30 seconds optimization interval, and there are 120 optimization cycles per hour (3600 seconds ÷ 30 seconds), then the average is 36 ÷ 120 = 0.3 decisions per cycle. The metric is wva_decisions_limited_total.
panels.title: Limiter Impact
How long a wake from zero took
panels.description: Distribution of wva_scale_from_zero_wake_seconds: from the first activation WVA published to the model being observed serving. Read the SHAPE, not the average. On FMA the same code path takes seconds when it binds a reusable sleeping instance and tens of seconds when it has to build one, so two bands is what a working warm pool looks like and the fast band thinning is how its regression appears - the wake still succeeds, just slowly, which is why nothing else reports it. A single slow band on a non-FMA model is simply the model load time and is expected.

panels.title: Wake from zero, p95 by model
panels.description: 95th percentile of wva_scale_from_zero_wake_seconds per model. The heatmap above shows whether the distribution is bimodal; this shows which model moved. A step change here with no config change is the warm pool having stopped being reusable - the case measured on pokprod, where a bind to a two-day-old sleeper took 59s against a 68s cold build because the sleeper was destroyed and rebuilt rather than reused.

panels.title: Serving: latency, queues and per-replica load (EPP + engine)
TTFT p95 (EPP)
panels.description:
Time to first token as the EPP measures it, per model.

model_name!="" is not decoration: the EPP records this histogram twice, once per model and once per flow-control flow (fairness_id, priority, streaming) with no model_name at all. Without the matcher the flow series forms its own group, and the panel draws a permanent NaN line legended as a nameless 'p95' and 'p50'.

panels.title: Inter-token latency p95 (EPP, normalized per output token)
panels.description:
Normalized time per output token -- the EPP's inter-token latency.

The `or` covers both builds: llm-d's EPP publishes llm_d_epp_request_ntpot_seconds, upstream publishes inference_objective_normalized_time_per_output_token_seconds. PromQL `or` takes the left where it has series and the right only where it does not.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model_name) (rate(llm_d_epp_request_ntpot_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m]))) or histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model_name) (rate(inference_objective_normalized_time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m])))

panels.title: EPP flow-control queue (requests queued at the router)
panels.description:
Requests held by flow control before they reach any engine.

This is where a backlog appears when the flowControl gate is on: the EPP admits only what an engine can absorb, so vllm:num_requests_waiting can read 0 while hundreds queue here. At zero replicas it is the ONLY evidence of demand, and it is what scale-from-zero wakes on.

panels.title: Waiting per replica (EPP per-endpoint queue)
panels.description:
Queue depth broken down per model-server replica, as the EPP sees it.

Engine-agnostic and per-replica at once, which no single engine metric gives: llm-d publishes llm_d_epp_per_endpoint_queue_size (keyed by model_server_endpoint), upstream publishes inference_pool_per_pod_queue_size (keyed by model_server_pod). Both are plotted; only one will have series on a given cluster.

panels.title: Running per replica (engine)
panels.description:
The one quantity the EPP does NOT break down per replica: it publishes llm_d_epp_request_running as a model-level total and inference_pool_average_running_requests as a pool average, but nothing per pod. So the per-replica series has to come from the engine, with vLLM and SGLang spelled differently and joined by `or`.

Aggregated max by (pod) so a replica scraped by two PodMonitors still draws one line.

panels.title: Pool KV-cache utilization (EPP)
panels.description:
Pool-average KV utilization as the EPP computes it, with the per-replica engine values alongside.

The average is what the scheduler routes on; the spread between it and the individual replicas is what tells you whether load is balanced.
